prompt:
Write an original fantasy story titled "The Orchard of Borrowed Rain".

Write this story in English.
Use third-person narration outside quoted speech and dreams.
Use past-tense narration outside quoted speech and dreams.
Preserve this physical rule: A glass seed releases rain only after a freely offered true memory; rain cannot revive a dead tree.
Follow the supplied three-chapter order.
Keep the memory book intact until its custody transfer in chapter three.
Keep Mael alive through the end of chapter three.
Present remembered scenes as past events rather than current events.

Use the supplied character, place and chronology bible. Let the unresolved questions develop through the supplied outline without treating a plan or dream as an event.

outline.title: Two Glass Seeds
outline.purpose: Develop The Orchard of Borrowed Rain through its planned state changes.
outline.turn: The village roll identified Mael as the appointed reeve.
hookSeeds: A seed rang softly without being touched.
A blank page remained warm inside the memory book.
Mael refused to remove a silver glove.

outline.title: The Dry Cistern
outline.purpose: Develop The Orchard of Borrowed Rain through its planned state changes.
outline.turn: The last living branch snapped; the old tree was dead.
hookSeeds: The ringing seed answered the bell inside the cistern.
The blank page was warm even in the cold cistern air.
A child’s name appeared beneath the cistern’s mineral crust.

outline.title: A Memory Freely Given
outline.purpose: Develop The Orchard of Borrowed Rain through its planned state changes.
outline.turn: A new sapling was alive beside the dead stump.
hookSeeds: The ringing seed held Orin’s freely offered memory.
The warm page returned the memory Mael had taken.
The glove concealed the scar of the former keeper.
The child’s name belonged to the memory’s rightful giver.

authorIntent: Let changing evidence alter trust without turning uncertainty into a completed event.
currentFocus: Preserve the difference between confirmed state, speech, recollection and conjecture.
